title: Frank Schiffman and the Apollo Theater circuit
summary: Schiffman owned the Apollo and the next stop was the Howard Theater; the black theater circuit.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: Yeah. Well, we'd like to get some of that on tape.
You also had some anecdotes about Frank Schiffman --
Who was the co-proprietor of the Apollo Theater.
Well, he was the out and out owner of the Apollo Theater, and had very much to do --
I read somewhere he had a partner by somebody named Brecher.
Brecher must've been the silent partner, because everybody knew the Apollo by --
It probably was part of a larger syndicate, because Schiffman -- the syndicate, I supposed, were part of the eastern, what they called 'seaboard' chain of theaters.
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943

When you worked the Apollo Theater, your next stop is the Howard Theater in Washington, D.C., and the Royal Theater in Baltimore. Now those were the three theaters that were known as the seaboard circuit.

There might've been some theaters in between, say like in Philadelphia, or some of the towns in between that I didn't know too much about, because -- although I did quite a lot of bit of vaudeville, I came in on the tail end of vaudeville and it was just about going out. And a lot of theaters had closed.
